chunks: Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Ayoub, from Al-Samyda, from Malik ibn Ayn al-Juhani, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

When two believers meet and shake hands, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, inserts His Hand between their two hands and turns His Face towards the one who loves his companion more intensely. So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, turns His Face upon them both, the sins fall away from them just as leaves fall from the tree.

key_terms.أَشَدِّهِمَا حُبّاً: The one who loves more intensely

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for two believers shaking hands?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the metaphysical reality of the handshake (muṣāfaha) as a conduit for divine mercy, where Allah’s face turns toward the believer who loves their companion more, signifying special favor. This act of divine attention causes sins to detach like falling leaves, a imagery often linked to the concept of tawbah (repentance) and the purifying nature of brotherhood in faith. It underscores the Shia emphasis on social bonds as a means of spiritual elevation and forgiveness.

en.hubeali:
Ibn Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from Ayoub, from Al Samyda, from Malik Bin Ayn Al Juhny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The Momineen, when two meet and shake hands, Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Inserts Hisazwj Hand between their two hands, and Turn by Hisazwj Face towards the one who has more intense love for his companions. So when Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Turns by Hisazwj Face upon them both, the sins erode from both of them just as the leaves erode from the tree’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ibn Faddal has narrated from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah from Ayyub from al-Sumayda’ from Malik ibn ‘A’Yun al-Juhni from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

‘When two believing people meet and shake hands Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, inserts His hand between their hands and faces the one whose love for his brother (in belief) is more intense. When Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, turns His face to them their sins begin to fall like leaves from trees.’”
